title: Maps from a finite-presentation module extend across a qc open
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $U\subseteq X$ be a quasi-compact open subscheme, let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $\mathcal G$ be an $\mathcal O_U$-module of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] (locally the cokernel of a map $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$ with $m,n$ finite), and let $\varphi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F|_U$ be $\mathcal O_U$-linear. Then there are a finite-presentation $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G'$ and an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\varphi':\mathcal G'\to\mathcal F$, together with an isomorphism $\mathcal G'|_U\cong\mathcal G$ under which $\varphi'|_U$ equals $\varphi$.

proof.text: *Step 1 (a finite affine cover and the opens $W_k$).* By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] every point of $X$ has an affine open neighbourhood; since $X$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], finitely many of these cover $X$. So there are affine opens $U_1,\dots,U_n\subseteq X$ with $X=U\cup U_1\cup\dots\cup U_n$ (Stacks takes $n$ minimal; any such finite family will do). Put $W_0=U$ and $W_k=U\cup U_1\cup\dots\cup U_k$ for $1\le k\le n$, so $W_n=X$. Each $U_i$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] and $U$ is quasi-compact by hypothesis, so each $W_k$, a finite union of quasi-compact subsets, is a quasi-compact open of $X$.

*Step 2 (the inductive claim).* For $0\le k\le n$ let $P(k)$ be the assertion: there are an $\mathcal O_{W_k}$-module $\mathcal G_k$ of finite presentation (locally on $W_k$ the cokernel of a map $\mathcal O^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O^{\oplus r}$, $m,r$ finite), an $\mathcal O_{W_k}$-linear map $\varphi_k:\mathcal G_k\to\mathcal F|_{W_k}$ and an $\mathcal O_U$-linear isomorphism $\alpha_k:\mathcal G_k|_U\to\mathcal G$ with $\varphi\circ\alpha_k=\varphi_k|_U$. $P(0)$ holds with $\mathcal G_0=\mathcal G$, $\varphi_0=\varphi$, $\alpha_0=\mathrm{id}$. $P(n)$ is the lemma, since $W_n=X$: take $\mathcal G'=\mathcal G_n$, $\varphi'=\varphi_n$ and the isomorphism $\alpha_n:\mathcal G'|_U\cong\mathcal G$, under which $\varphi'|_U$ corresponds to $\varphi$. Steps 3-9 prove $P(k)\Rightarrow P(k+1)$ for $0\le k<n$; this is Stacks' reduction to the case $X=U\cup V$ with $V$ affine, applied to the pair $(W_k,U_{k+1})$ inside $X$ (so that only quasi-compactness of $W_k$ and quasi-separatedness of $X$ are needed, not quasi-separatedness of $W_{k+1}$).

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PI proof, first and second paragraphs (lines 2963-2989)

proof.text: *Step 3 (the affine situation).* Assume $P(k)$, $k<n$, and put $V=U_{k+1}$, an affine open, and $U'=W_k\cap V$. Since $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, its underlying space is spectral [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral], so the intersection of two quasi-compact open subsets of $X$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-spectral-space]. As $W_k$ and $V$ are quasi-compact opens (Step 1), $U'$ is a quasi-compact open. For every affine open $W\subseteq V$, $W$ is a quasi-compact open of $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] and $U'\cap W=W_k\cap W$ is quasi-compact by the same fact; so the inclusion $U'\to V$ is quasi-compact. $V$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. $\mathcal F|_V$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_V$-module [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](2). Put $\mathcal G''=\mathcal G_k|_{U'}$ and $\varphi''=\varphi_k|_{U'}:\mathcal G''\to\mathcal F|_{U'}$. $\mathcal G''$ is of finite presentation (the local presentations of $\mathcal G_k$ restrict to opens of $U'$), hence quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](0).

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PI proof, second paragraph (lines 2977-2989): the system $(V,U\cap V,\mathcal F|_V,\mathcal G|_{U\cap V},\varphi|_{U\cap V})$

proof.text: *Step 4 (a quasi-coherent extension, Lemma 01PE).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-extension-qc-open] to the scheme $V$, its open $U'$ (with quasi-compact inclusion, Step 3), the quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_V$-module $\mathcal F|_V$, the quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{U'}$-module $\mathcal G''$ and $\varphi''$: there are a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_V$-module $\mathcal H$, an $\mathcal O_V$-linear $\psi:\mathcal H\to\mathcal F|_V$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:\mathcal H|_{U'}\to\mathcal G''$ with $\varphi''\circ\alpha=\psi|_{U'}$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PI proof, third paragraph (lines 2991-2995), using Lemma 01PE (3)

proof.text: *Step 5 (making $\mathcal H$ of finite type, Lemma 01PF).* $\mathcal H|_{U'}\cong\mathcal G''$ is of finite presentation, hence of finite type [pqf-def-coherent] (a local presentation $\mathcal O^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal H|_{U'}\to0$ contains a surjection $\mathcal O^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal H|_{U'}$ on the same open), and it is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](2). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-submodule-extension] to the quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme $V$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], its quasi-compact open $U'$, the quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_V$-module $\mathcal H$ and the finite type quasi-coherent submodule $\mathcal H|_{U'}\subseteq\mathcal H|_{U'}$: there is a quasi-coherent finite type submodule $\mathcal H'\subseteq\mathcal H$ with $\mathcal H'|_{U'}=\mathcal H|_{U'}$. Let $\psi':\mathcal H'\to\mathcal F|_V$ be the restriction of $\psi$ to $\mathcal H'$. Since $\mathcal H'|_{U'}=\mathcal H|_{U'}$, still $\alpha:\mathcal H'|_{U'}\to\mathcal G''$ is an isomorphism with $\varphi''\circ\alpha=\psi'|_{U'}$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PI proof, third paragraph (lines 2995-3000), using Lemma 01PF

proof.text: *Step 6 (a surjection $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal H'$ and its kernel).* $V$ is affine and $\mathcal H'$ is quasi-coherent of finite type, so there are finitely many global sections $h_1,\dots,h_m\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal H')$ which generate $\mathcal H'$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-finite-type-generating-sections], i.e. $\pi:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal H'$, $(f_j)\mapsto\sum_jf_jh_j$, is surjective as a map of sheaves [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], hence an epimorphism of $\Mod(\mathcal O_V)$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting](1). (Stacks: $\mathcal H'=\widetilde N$ with $N$ finitely generated; the cited node is this fact, Properties 01PB, in the form needed.) Let $\mathcal K=\Ker\pi$, the sectionwise kernel [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}$ is of finite presentation (presentation $0\to\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}$), hence quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](0), so $\mathcal K$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel]. This is the short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal K\to\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal H'\to0$ of the source.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PI proof, third paragraph (lines 3000-3008); the source cites Lemma lemma-finite-presentation-module (01PC) here, the fact used is Lemma lemma-finite-type-module (01PB)

proof.text: *Step 7 ($\mathcal K|_{U'}$ is of finite type and extends, Modules 01BP and Lemma 01PF).* Kernels are sectionwise, so $\Ker(\pi|_{U'})=\mathcal K|_{U'}$; and $\pi|_{U'}:\mathcal O_{U'}^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal H'|_{U'}$ is surjective as a map of sheaves (the condition of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting](1) for opens inside $U'$ is part of that for $\pi$), hence an epimorphism. Its target $\mathcal H'|_{U'}=\mathcal H|_{U'}\cong\mathcal G''$ is of finite presentation. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-kernel-surjection-finite-type] on the ringed space $(U',\mathcal O_{U'})$, $\mathcal K|_{U'}$ is of finite type; it is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](2). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-submodule-extension] to $V$ (quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]), $U'$, the quasi-coherent $\mathcal K$ and the submodule $\mathcal K|_{U'}\subseteq\mathcal K|_{U'}$: there is a quasi-coherent finite type submodule $\mathcal K'\subseteq\mathcal K$ with $\mathcal K'|_{U'}=\mathcal K|_{U'}$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PI proof, fourth paragraph (lines 3010-3018), using Modules, Lemma 01BP and Lemma 01PF

proof.text: *Step 8 (the finitely presented module over $V$ and its map).* Let $q:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal G'_V$ be the cokernel in $\Mod(\mathcal O_V)$ of the inclusion $\mathcal K'\to\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Since $\mathcal K'$ is of finite type and $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}$ of finite presentation, $\mathcal G'_V$ is of finite presentation [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-presentation-cokernel]. Since $\mathcal K'\subseteq\mathcal K=\Ker\pi$, $\pi$ kills $\mathcal K'$, so there is a unique $\rho:\mathcal G'_V\to\mathcal H'$ with $\rho\circ q=\pi$; put $\varphi'_V=\psi'\circ\rho:\mathcal G'_V\to\mathcal F|_V$ (the composition $\mathcal O^{\oplus m}/\mathcal K'\to\mathcal O^{\oplus m}/\mathcal K=\mathcal H'\xrightarrow{\psi'}\mathcal F|_V$ of the source). Restriction to $U'$ preserves cokernels [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](1), so $q|_{U'}$ is a cokernel of $\mathcal K'|_{U'}=\mathcal K|_{U'}=\Ker(\pi|_{U'})\to\mathcal O_{U'}^{\oplus m}$, and $\rho|_{U'}$ is the map from this cokernel induced by $\pi|_{U'}$. As $\pi|_{U'}$ is an epimorphism (Step 7) and $\Mod(\mathcal O_{U'})$ is abelian, an epimorphism is the cokernel of its kernel, so $\rho|_{U'}$ is an isomorphism. Hence $\beta=\alpha\circ\rho|_{U'}:\mathcal G'_V|_{U'}\to\mathcal G''=\mathcal G_k|_{U'}$ is an isomorphism, and $\varphi_k|_{U'}\circ\beta=\varphi''\circ\alpha\circ\rho|_{U'}=\psi'|_{U'}\circ\rho|_{U'}=\varphi'_V|_{U'}$.

*Step 9 (glueing over $W_{k+1}=W_k\cup V$).* $W_{k+1}=W_k\cup V$ with $W_k\cap V=U'$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules](2) to the ringed space $W_{k+1}$ with the covering $\{W_k,V\}$, the modules $\mathcal G_k$ on $W_k$ and $\mathcal G'_V$ on $V$, and the isomorphisms $\beta^{-1}:\mathcal G_k|_{U'}\to\mathcal G'_V|_{U'}$, $\beta$ in the other direction and the identities on $W_k$ and on $V$; the cocycle condition holds since for indices in $\{W_k,V\}$ it reduces to $\beta\circ\beta^{-1}=\mathrm{id}$, $\beta^{-1}\circ\beta=\mathrm{id}$ or identities. This gives an $\mathcal O_{W_{k+1}}$-module $\mathcal G_{k+1}$ and isomorphisms $\gamma_1:\mathcal G_{k+1}|_{W_k}\to\mathcal G_k$, $\gamma_2:\mathcal G_{k+1}|_V\to\mathcal G'_V$ with $\beta^{-1}\circ\gamma_1|_{U'}=\gamma_2|_{U'}$. $\mathcal G_{k+1}$ is of finite presentation: every point of $W_{k+1}$ lies in $W_k$ or in $V$, where $\mathcal G_{k+1}$ is isomorphic to the finitely presented $\mathcal G_k$ resp. $\mathcal G'_V$ (Step 8), and the local presentations transfer along the isomorphisms. The maps $\varphi_k\circ\gamma_1:\mathcal G_{k+1}|_{W_k}\to\mathcal F|_{W_k}$ and $\varphi'_V\circ\gamma_2:\mathcal G_{k+1}|_V\to\mathcal F|_V$ agree on $U'$: $\varphi'_V|_{U'}\circ\gamma_2|_{U'}=\varphi_k|_{U'}\circ\beta\circ\beta^{-1}\circ\gamma_1|_{U'}=\varphi_k|_{U'}\circ\gamma_1|_{U'}$ (Step 8). By [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules](1) there is a unique $\mathcal O_{W_{k+1}}$-linear $\varphi_{k+1}:\mathcal G_{k+1}\to\mathcal F|_{W_{k+1}}$ restricting to these. Put $\alpha_{k+1}=\alpha_k\circ\gamma_1|_U:\mathcal G_{k+1}|_U\to\mathcal G$ (note $U\subseteq W_k$); then $\varphi\circ\alpha_{k+1}=\varphi_k|_U\circ\gamma_1|_U=\varphi_{k+1}|_U$. This is $P(k+1)$, which completes the induction of Step 2.

split_report.summary: Read Stacks Properties 01PI (lemma-extend-finite-presentation, properties.tex 2963-3030) with 01PE, 01PF, Modules 01BO/01BP/0H96. Wrote the proof in 9 steps: finite affine cover and opens W_k (1), the inductive claim P(k) with base and conclusion (2), the affine situation V=U_{k+1}, U'=W_k cap V with quasi-compactness of U' and of the inclusion U'->V via the Mathlib leaves lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral and def-weil-spectral-space (3), quasi-coherent extension by 01PE (4), finite type replacement by 01PF (5), surjection O^m->H' and its quasi-coherent kernel (6), K|_{U'} finite type by 01BP and its extension K' by 01PF (7), G'_V = O^m/K' finitely presented by the cokernel node and the iso on U' (8), glueing modules and maps over W_{k+1} (9). The induction is set up on W_k inside X rather than by Stacks' 'reduce to n=1' on the scheme W_{k+1}, which avoids needing W_{k+1} quasi-separated. Removed the two lemmas from stmt_deps (they are proof tools, now in the steps) and added def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme. New nodes: lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-extension-qc-open (01PE (3), unsplit) and lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs (Mathlib leaf). Source slip: 01PI cites lemma-finite-presentation-module (01PC) where lemma-finite-type-module (01PB) is meant; it also leaves implicit that a finitely presented G is quasi-coherent (needed for 01PE) and that U cap V -> V is quasi-compact.

reviewed.note: 9 steps following Stacks 01PI as an induction on W_k = U cup U_1 cup ... cup U_k inside the qcqs X: finite affine cover; the inductive claim; the affine situation with U' = W_k cap V quasi-compact (spectral-space leaf, new leaf: affine schemes are qcqs, AffineScheme.lean:561 / QuasiSeparated.lean:167 verified by L); quasi-coherent extension (new unsplit 01PE (3) node); finite-type submodule (01PF node); a surjection from O_V^m and its kernel; the kernel over U' is of finite type (01BP node) and extends; the cokernel is finitely presented (today's 0H96 node) and agrees with G_k on U'; gluing. Source: 01PI cites 01PC where 01PB is used, and leaves the quasi-coherence of G and the quasi-compactness of U cap V -> V unstated. The two tool lemmas were removed from stmt_deps (they are proof tools); L added the citation of def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finitePresentation_extension (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X)) (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (G : SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U)) [G.IsFinitePresentation] (φ : G ⟶ F.over U) : ∃ (G' : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)), G'.IsFinitePresentation ∧ ∃ (φ' : G' ⟶ F) (e : G'.over U ≅ G), (SheafOfModules.overFunctor (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).map φ' = e.hom ≫ φ
